svg.title: What shared exclusions always is, and what it is not
svg.desc: Properties that hold for every finite law, such as well-defined events, likelihood-ratio cumulatives and an exact decomposition, next to popular readings that are false.

g.font-family: 'Source Sans Pro', 'Source Sans 3', 'Latin Modern Math', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
g.text: WHAT SHARED EXCLUSIONS ALWAYS IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT
Holds for every finite law
Popular readings that are false
Events are well defined
Every event contains the observed row, so it has positive probability.
Cumulatives are likelihood ratios
Each is log P(t | E) / P(t), an ordinary information value for one event.
The decomposition is exact
Order, event inclusions and Möbius inversion give signed atoms with
no remainder.
Atoms add up to the total
The top event is the full source state; for the AND gate the atoms add
up to Hbin(1/4) = 0.5623 nats.
Components are nonnegative
Informative and misinformative atoms are ≥ 0 (MGW); net atoms may
be negative.
Relabeling changes nothing
Swapping sources or re-encoding one source's values leaves every
event, hence every atom, unchanged.
Independent sources share nothing
Two independent bits copied into T = (S1, S2) give Red = log 4/3 =
0.288 nats.
Atoms are nonnegative amounts
Exclusive or gives Red = log 2/3 = −0.405 nats.
Pairwise laws determine the atoms
Exclusive or and a target independent of both sources have the same
pairwise laws; the first has nonzero atoms, the second all zero.
Roles or coarsening do not matter
Atoms are not symmetric in the roles of sources and target, and
coarsening a source or the target can raise net redundancy.
Shannon theory forces the OR event
The OR of agreements is a chosen notion of shared logical
consequence; other PIDs choose differently.
The average is one variable's information
The event moves with the observed row, so no fixed auxiliary variable
carries the average.
Measure: categorical shared exclusions (Makkeh, Gutknecht and Wibral 2021). Witness values computed exactly.
